title: Every integrable weight is weyl conjugate toward the dominant chamber
statement: For an integral weight of an integrable module whose Weyl orbit meets the dominant chamber, successive reflections at negative simple labels reach the dominant representative; chamber boundary stabilizers must be treated. For integrable highest-weight modules every weight orbit meets that chamber.
strategy: The highest-weight/O clause has a complete height route: a negative label reflection strictly raises the weight and the finite set of support weights above the initial weight bounds the iteration. The general conditional orbit clause and uniqueness/stabilizer need the dual positive-root inversion lemma and reduced-word exchange; these are absent from RL12 and the empty DG root-systems planned page. Kleshchev Proposition 3.4.1 uses Lemma 3.3.2 and its dual, not merely root preservation. Preserve claim and escalate until this local Coxeter interface has a complete scaffold and proof; do not claim all arbitrary integrable weight orbits meet the chamber.
source_locators: Kleshchev Proposition 3.4.1 pp47–48 and Corollary 10.1.3 p128; Perrin Corollary 10.5.4 p89
